inputs_used.note: Used parent-staged paths only; inputs folder not overwritten

body_mask.meaning: grayscale luminance mask: white/high = inside body, black/low = outside; NOT RGBA transparency
body_mask.identity_note: Body mask L channel is byte-identical to master RGBA alpha (max abs diff 0). It is a luminance export of the master alpha, not an independent hand-traced matte.

eye_nose_mask.meaning: grayscale luminance mask for eyes+nose features
eye_nose_mask.placement: Eye/nose mask (>=128) sits almost entirely in master alpha holes: 1934/2006 px where master alpha==0; remaining 72 are soft alpha 1-119. Zero overlap with body>=128. Intended as fill-into-cutouts layer, complementary to body mask.

alignment_metrics.threshold: body>=128 vs master_alpha>=128, native coords, no resize

feature_coverage_notes.interpretation_hint: If bright teeth/claws/highlights are inside body mask, coat fills will cover them unless a separate protect mask is used. Eye/nose mask is separate for feature coloring.

pass_fail_rationale.criteria: PASS if same canvas, IoU>=0.99, spill<0.5% of body, missing<1% of master, and interior hard mismatches small

mask_limitations: Body mask is mode L (luminance), not RGBA; renderer should use L as coverage (or treat as alpha).
Body mask L is byte-identical to master alpha — useful as reusable coverage, but not an independent matte.
Eyes and nose are cut out of master alpha / body mask (holes). Coat fills using body mask will not paint those pixels; use eye/nose mask (or RGB already in master holes) for those features.
Body mask / master alpha INCLUDE sabers (teeth) and claws / paw mass. Coat color fills will tint sabers and claws unless a separate protect/exclude mask is added later.
Eye/nose mask is mode L with 3 connected components (2 eye-related + 1 nose). It is complementary to body (no overlap at >=128).
Master shows typical AA fringe / light halo at fur tips against contrasting backgrounds; this is in the artwork alpha, not a mask registration error.
Very-bright opaque pixels (lum>=245): 372, all inside body — consistent with sabers/claws/highlights being body-covered.

visual_inspection.method: Read() on comparison sheet, silhouette overlap, and landmark crops at native coordinates
visual_inspection.overall: PASS. Master and body silhouette register with no visible offset at face, sabers, paws, shoulder, or fur edge. No material red spill or blue missing in overlay. Eye/nose magenta lands in the facial cutouts.

landmarks.face: Cutouts at eyes/nose align with features; sabers included in body; magenta eye/nose overlays register on sockets/nose leather; no offset.
landmarks.sabers_mouth: Both sabers present in body mask as solid coverage; curvature matches master; anti-alias fringe only.
landmarks.front_paws: Paw mass and claw silhouettes follow master; claws are inside master alpha (=body). Thin AA fringe only, not material spill.
landmarks.hind_paws: Generated; silhouette agreement expected identical given byte-equal alpha.
landmarks.shoulder: Generated; no mismatch expected given identity.
landmarks.fur_edge_left: Jagged fur fringe matches; soft AA halo on master against dark/checker is premultiplied-looking fringe in the artwork alpha itself, not mask misalignment (mask==alpha).
landmarks.eye_nose_comp1_near_eye: Largest eye-adjacent component sits in cutout; minor soft-edge partials only.
landmarks.eye_nose_comp3_nose: Nose leather hole filled by eye/nose mask; aligns with cutout.

visual_inspection.fringe_vs_material: Hard spill/missing at threshold 128: 0 px. Soft channels identical. Any visible halo is anti-alias content inside the shared alpha, not a coordinate mismatch between mask and master.

recommendation: Safe to proceed with a layered renderer that composites on the shared 1448x1086 canvas, using master as immutable base, body L as coat coverage, and eye/nose L as feature fills into cutouts. Do not regenerate or reshape the master. Consider a future protect mask if sabers/claws must stay untinted by coat fills.
